name: Freelance graphic designer (contests and 1-to-1 projects)
summary: Apply to 99designs as a designer, then compete in client design contests (only the winner is paid) or take 1-to-1 projects. Since January 2026 all payouts go through Hyperwallet.
what_you_do: After a curated application you enter contests, where many designers submit concepts for one brief and only the chosen winner is paid, or you work directly with clients on 1-to-1 projects at prices you set. Contest prizes are credited after the client approves the handover and a five-business-day review.
who_it_may_fit: You already have professional design skills and a portfolio and can afford unpaid contest entries while building a reputation.
Clients come to the platform, so there is less self-marketing than going solo
99designs says clients must fund a contest before it launches, so a won prize is backed by money already paid in
who_it_may_not_fit: You need dependable income or object to speculative (unpaid) work.
Losing contest entries are unpaid; third-party reviews describe poor odds in contests with many entrants
Acceptance is curated and competitive (v1 claim; application page not re-seen in October 2026)
A verified Hyperwallet account with government ID is mandatory; designers without one were suspended after 19 January 2026
Minimum payout is $25 (currency not stated in the snippet); smaller balances wait
No page seen names Canada as an eligible designer country

name: Stock photo, video & illustration contributor
summary: Upload photos, video, vectors or illustrations to Adobe Stock and earn 33% (35% for video) of the net licence price each time a customer licenses them. Many downloads pay under US$1.
what_you_do: You create and upload assets with titles and keywords through the contributor portal; files are moderated and accepted ones earn a royalty per licence. Income builds slowly from a back catalogue and depends on buyers finding your files in a very large library.
who_it_may_fit: You already produce photos, footage or vector art and want a small, slow side income without counting on it.
Published royalty rate: 33% for photos, vectors and illustrations, 35% for video
No required training; you work whenever you like
who_it_may_not_fit: You need predictable income soon.
Per-item minimums on large subscription plans start at US$0.33 per download
Contributors on Adobe's forum (2026, anecdotal) report sharp, unexplained drops in sales and blame AI-generated competition; one reports steady growth by uploading about 100 assets a month
Payout rules (US$25 minimum, 45-day wait, PayPal/Payoneer/Skrill, 18+, country fixed at Adobe ID creation, 30% withholding without a tax form) are v1 claims not re-seen in October 2026

eligibility_notes: No page seen names Canada. Inferred from a global contributor program whose royalties are computed on the US purchase price for all contributors; v1 cited Adobe's payment-requirements page (PayPal available globally), not re-seen this round.

other: AI-generated content must be labelled as such (third-party 2026 guide)

conditions_notes: Income depends on buyer downloads, not hours worked.

advertised_rate.note: Per-item minimum royalty of US$0.33 per download on Large Subscription plans (0–999 lifetime licences of a standard asset); standard rate 33% of the net licence price for photos, vectors and illustrations and 35% for video, based on the US purchase price after discounts. No typical monthly income is published.

fees: No upfront or subscription fees (v1 claim from Adobe's overview page, not re-seen).
payment_terms: v1 claims not re-seen: US$25 minimum balance, 45 days after first sale, payout via PayPal, Payoneer or Skrill.
unpaid_work: All production and keywording is unpaid until a file sells.
economics_notes: Custom agreements and non-standard plans pay 33%/35% of the attributable amount or a flat rate (official royalty page).

name: Film & TV production assistant (category)
summary: Entry-level on-set crew work (NOC 53111) reached through word of mouth, guild training and occasional city-funded programs. Job Bank rates Ontario's 2025–2027 outlook Very limited, with Ontario wages of $18–$38 an hour (median $24).
what_you_do: Production assistants support crews on set and on location: running errands, moving and setting up equipment, managing people and traffic around the set, distributing paperwork and helping whichever department needs a hand. Work is on-site, by the day or by production, with long and irregular days.
how_to_find_work: Search Job Bank and Indeed for 'production assistant', 'set PA' and 'office PA' in Toronto, Hamilton, Ottawa and Northern Ontario, but expect few public postings: an Indeed search for 'production assistant film' in Toronto on 13 October 2026 returned nothing, and most PA hiring goes through production coordinators and personal referrals. Training routes that have fed PA hiring: the Directors Guild of Canada – Ontario (a member profile cites a 2024 'GAP' set-PA course; the Guild earlier counted a City of Toronto/POV PA program toward its apprenticeship), and free northern Ontario crew workshops run by Cultural Industries Ontario North with REEL Canada (2023). Check those organizations directly for 2026–27 intakes, none of which was confirmed.
who_it_may_fit: You like fast-paced, physical teamwork on location and can take long days at short notice.
Job Bank's Toronto Region summary describes good prospects even though the province-wide outlook is Very limited
Job Bank Ontario wages: $18.00 low, $24.00 median, $38.00 high per hour (Toronto median $27.00)
who_it_may_not_fit: You need remote work, regular hours or steady weekly income.

Job Bank: 2025–2027 outlook Very limited in Ontario (moderate growth, few retirements, several unemployed workers with recent experience); national outlook flags a strong risk of labour surplus 2024–2033
Part-time and seasonal work is common; Job Bank says only 19% of workers in this occupation work all year
Wage data is from 2023–2024
The training programs found (Toronto PA program for Black young adults 18–29; northern Ontario workshops) date from 2019–2023; no 2026 intake was confirmed

eligibility_notes: Ordinary Ontario employment; Job Bank publishes Ontario-specific outlook and wages for the occupation.

requirements.education: No formal requirement for PA work in practice; Job Bank's occupational group usually expects a college diploma, apprenticeship or 6+ months on-the-job training (v1 wording not re-seen)
other: Driver's licence is often expected for runner roles (general industry practice; not from a source seen)

conditions_notes: Project-based day work; income follows local filming activity.

advertised_rate.note: Job Bank 'Production Assistant' Ontario wages: $18.00 low, $24.00 median, $38.00 high per hour (2023–2024 data); Toronto Region median $27.00, Windsor-Sarnia $19.20, Stratford–Bruce Peninsula $23.50. Employee wages; day rates on sets not verified.

name: Stock photo, video & illustration contributor
summary: Upload images or footage to Shutterstock and earn 15%–40% of each licence depending on a level that resets to 15% every 1 January; some downloads pay only the US$0.10 minimum.
what_you_do: You create and keyword images, footage or vectors and submit them for review; approved files earn a royalty per download. Levels (six each for images and video) rise with the current calendar year's downloads only, so every contributor restarts at Level 1 each January.
who_it_may_fit: You already make saleable photos, video or illustrations and want a passive outlet without relying on the money.
Free to join; payouts via PayPal, Skrill or Payoneer once you have US$25
Payments go out between the 7th and 15th of each month
who_it_may_not_fit: You need predictable or near-term income.
Level 1 pays 15% of the sale (up to 100 licences a year); 40% needs more than 25,000 licences in a year, and levels reset every 1 January
Some downloads pay a flat US$0.10 because the percentage would be less
An approved tax form is required before any payment; contributors from certain countries face a 90-day waiting period (countries not listed)

Trustpilot reviewers (2025, anecdotal) describe accounts closed with earnings held; Shutterstock says closure can take up to 90 days and it holds earnings when a payment provider stops serving a region

eligibility_notes: No page names Canada. Shutterstock's payment help says non-US contributors are paid once a tax form is approved, and only Russia/Belarus restrictions were seen.

other: Approved tax form (W-8BEN for non-US contributors, per v1; form name not re-seen)

conditions_notes: Income depends on buyer downloads; the annual level reset lowers everyone's rate each January.

advertised_rate.note: US$0.10 minimum per download; otherwise 15% (Level 1, up to 100 licences in the calendar year) rising to 40% (Level 6, over 25,000 licences) of the sale price; video levels use different thresholds. No typical monthly income is published.

fees: Free to join. Minimum payout $25, maximum $2,000 per payout; payments under $1 cannot be issued.
payment_terms: PayPal, Skrill or Payoneer; payments sent between the 7th and 15th of the month.
Approved tax form required for US and non-US contributors before payment.
unpaid_work: All production and keywording is unpaid until a file sells.
economics_notes: A promotional comparison blog (2026) and a Polish article describe contributor dissatisfaction with the annual reset ('30% pay cut' for mid-level contributors); anecdotal.

risk_notes: Account closures with earnings held are individual Trustpilot claims (2025), not verified cases.

name: Social media coordinator / community manager (category)
summary: Planning, posting and monitoring social content for an organization, as an employee or freelancer. Job Bank Ontario: median $37.02 an hour, prospects 'limited', a university degree usual. Fake 'social media task' jobs are a major fraud.
what_you_do: You plan and schedule posts, write captions, make simple graphics or short clips, answer comments and messages and report engagement. Employees sit in marketing or communications teams; freelancers run accounts for several small businesses or creators.
how_to_find_work: Search Indeed and Job Bank for 'social media coordinator', 'social media & content specialist', 'marketing coordinator' and 'communications coordinator': an Indeed Ontario search on 13 October 2026 showed current postings in Toronto (CWB Group), Scarborough (e11ement), Guelph, Markham, Kitchener and smaller towns, most of them marketing-coordinator roles that include social media. Pitch small businesses, nonprofits and real-estate teams directly with examples of accounts you have grown; for freelance work use the catalogue's Upwork and Fiverr records. Treat any offer that asks you to pay, buy crypto or 'unlock' tasks as fraud.
who_it_may_fit: You write well, enjoy online communities and simple visuals, and can show results in a portfolio.
Job Bank Ontario wages (updated 19 Nov 2025): $20.00 low, $37.02 median, $58.97 high per hour; Toronto median $37.50
87.8% of Ontario workers in the occupation get at least one non-wage benefit (Job Bank)
Much of the work is remote and written

name: App-based food and grocery delivery courier (category)
summary: Delivering food, groceries or parcels for apps such as DoorDash, Uber Eats, Instacart or SkipTheDishes as an independent contractor. Since 1 July 2025 Ontario's Digital Platform Workers' Rights Act guarantees minimum wage only for 'engaged' time; waiting time is unpaid and vehicle costs are yours.
what_you_do: You sign up in a platform app, pass identity and background checks, then accept delivery offers by car, bike or on foot, often during meal peaks. Pay is per delivery plus tips; you cover fuel, maintenance, insurance and phone costs and handle your own taxes.
how_to_find_work: Sign up directly in the courier apps operating in your city (DoorDash, Uber Eats, Instacart, SkipTheDishes; their sign-up pages were not opened this round) and choose a vehicle type suited to your area, since bikes and e-bikes work only in dense cores. Before relying on it, read Ontario's Digital Platform Workers' Rights Act, 2022 (in force 1 July 2025): minimum wage applies to time on an assigned task only, tips are on top, and the Act does not cover overtime or holiday pay. Track every expense for tax; test a few weeks and compute your real hourly rate after costs.
who_it_may_fit: You have a reliable vehicle or bike, want work you can start within days and can accept pay that varies by hour and season.
Ontario law now sets a minimum wage floor for engaged time plus tips (DPWRA, in force 1 July 2025)
Low barrier to entry; no interview
who_it_may_not_fit: You need predictable income or cannot absorb vehicle costs.
Only engaged time is paid at minimum wage; waiting between offers is not

Effective earnings after expenses are often low: a 2023 RideFairTO study estimated Toronto Uber drivers netted about $7.90/hour after roughly $12/hour in vehicle costs (about $20/hour gross); Uber countered with a $33.98 median for engaged time. Toronto couriers interviewed by Now Toronto (undated) said about $20/hour at busy times before expenses. No 2026 Ontario courier survey was found
Critics (Globe and Mail) say the engaged-time rule lets platforms cut effective wages; the Act does not cover overtime, holiday pay or emergency leave
Independent-contractor status: no EI, CPP employer share or paid leave

eligibility_notes: Platforms require proof of work eligibility and ID (not verified this round). Ontario-specific rights under the DPWRA apply to ride-share, delivery and courier platform work in the province.

certifications: Driver's licence and insurance for car delivery
other: Background check (platform practice; not verified this round)

conditions_notes: Offer volume follows meal peaks and weather; you can log on any time but may wait unpaid between offers.

anecdotal_effective_rate.basis: RideFairTO 2023 estimate for Toronto Uber rideshare drivers after vehicle costs ($7.90/hour; about $20/hour before costs) and undated Now Toronto interviews with couriers reporting about $20/hour at busy times before expenses. Not 2026 courier data; generic 2026 sites claim $15–$25/hour before and $12–$20 after expenses without methodology.

payment_terms: Platform payout schedules not verified this round.
unpaid_work: Waiting time between offers is unpaid under the DPWRA.
economics_notes: DPWRA minimum wage applies per assigned task, in addition to tips; a law-firm blog cited $17.20/hour 'as of Oct 1 2025', which does not match the current Ontario rate schedule and was not relied on. Check ontario.ca for the rate in force.

required_purchases: Vehicle or bike, insurance, phone plan
potential_expenses: Fuel, maintenance, parking tickets, commercial-use insurance rider

risk_notes: Effective-earnings evidence is from rideshare (2023) and undated courier interviews, not a 2026 Ontario courier study.
barriers: Vehicle costs and insurance; dense-area demand.
contradictions: RideFairTO's $7.90/hour net estimate vs Uber's $33.98/hour engaged-time median (different bases: after costs and all time vs gross engaged time).

name: Non-lawyer notary public / commissioner for taking affidavits (Ontario)
summary: Considered as a licensed microbusiness route and rejected: Ontario appoints non-lawyer notaries only when an applicant's existing employer needs documents notarized, and states appointments are not granted to start a new line of business.
what_you_do: A notary public certifies documents and takes affidavits; a commissioner for taking affidavits administers oaths and takes affidavits and statutory declarations. In Ontario, lawyers and paralegals get notary status through the Law Society route; everyone else must apply to the Ministry of the Attorney General's Legal Appointments Office.
how_to_find_work: Not a route an individual can start on their own: the Ministry of the Attorney General considers non-lawyer notary applications only when your employment requires notarizing documents, needs a letter of authorization from your employer and a CPIC criminal record check, and says appointments are not granted to let applicants enter a new line of business. Commissioner-for-taking-affidavits appointments use a separate general application and the same office. The realistic paths are to hold a job that needs the appointment, or to become a licensed paralegal or lawyer.
who_it_may_fit: You already work for an organization that needs documents notarized or commissioned and your employer will sponsor the application.
who_it_may_not_fit: You want to open an independent notary or commissioner service: Ontario says appointments are not granted for that purpose.
Non-lawyer notary appointment fee $110, three-year term, 4–6 weeks processing; commissioner fee not published online (call the Legal Appointments Office)
audience_restriction: Employees whose job requires notarizing or commissioning documents; licensed lawyers and paralegals

eligibility_notes: Not eligible as an independent route: appointments go only to applicants whose Ontario employer needs the appointment, or to Ontario lawyers and paralegals.

certifications: Ministry of the Attorney General appointment (non-lawyer) or Law Society licence (lawyer/paralegal)
other: Employer letter of authorization on letterhead; CPIC criminal record check (non-lawyer notary)

conditions_notes: Appointment is tied to employment; it does not create independent work.

fees: $110 application fee for a non-lawyer notary appointment payable to the Minister of Finance (waived for certain government employees; band councils added as fee-exempt from 1 January 2026 under Reg. 831).
economics_notes: Fee regulation R.R.O. 1990, Reg. 831 under the Notaries Act sets appointment fees.

barriers: Requires employer sponsorship; cannot be used to start a business.
